title: Fort Laramie
paragraphs: An adult Western drama set around a U.S. Army post on the frontier, following soldiers and civilians through the dangers, hardships, and moral conflicts of life in the West.
Adult frontier Western centered on Captain Lee Quince and the soldiers/civilians around a U.S. Army post.
The run breaks into several distinct periods: CBS regular run (January 22, 1956 to October 28, 1956) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include [[person|raymond-burr|Raymond Burr]] (performer), Kathleen Hite (writer), Norman Macdonnell (producer and director), Amerigo Moreno (music supervisor), Bill James (sound patterns), [[person|jack-moyles|Jack Moyles]] (performer), and [[person|john-dehner|John Dehner]] (performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]], [[org|org.cd82fd99edb39caa|Armed Forces Radio and Television Service]], and [[org|org.86a7ba0f309a63c9|WEEI]].

The stories often return to frontier Army-post life, military duty and discipline, soldier-civilian frontier relations, family, wives and widows at the post, recruits, training and soldiering, and stagecoach, scouting and frontier travel.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Adult Western drama in late-network radio, Frontier Army-post setting, 1950s radio portrayals of Native/frontier relations, and CBS sustaining drama.

An adult Western drama set around a U.S. Army post on the frontier, following soldiers and civilians through the dangers, hardships, and moral conflicts of life in the West.

Adult frontier Western centered on Captain Lee Quince and the soldiers/civilians around a U.S. Army post.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: CBS regular run (January 22, 1956 to October 28, 1956) on CBS Radio Network.

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Raymond Burr (performer), Kathleen Hite (writer), Norman Macdonnell (producer and director), Amerigo Moreno (music supervisor), Bill James (sound patterns), Jack Moyles (performer), and John Dehner (performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to CBS Radio Network, Armed Forces Radio and Television Service, and WEEI.

The stories often return to frontier Army-post life, military duty and discipline, soldier-civilian frontier relations, family, wives and widows at the post, recruits, training and soldiering, and stagecoach, scouting and frontier travel.

The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Adult Western drama in late-network radio, Frontier Army-post setting, 1950s radio portrayals of Native/frontier relations, and CBS sustaining drama.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include Gunsmoke, Escape, Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar, Have Gun, Will Travel, and Lux Radio Theatre.
